thread:
samuel: Heads-up — canary for the invoke-gateway strict-validate rollout started throwing a bunch of rejects around 10:12 UTC in us-east-1. Reject rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~4.5% after the flag flip. Raising to eng-platform to triage.
kevin: Which validator? Is this fncall or toolhook validation? Any sample payloads/log lines?
rita: It looks like structured output validator for fncall responses. Console traces show error "schema_mismatch: unexpected_field_type" and the payloads are mostly tiny assistant-to-tool replies with an array where object expected. Happening across multiple customers but concentrated on a single model variant.
samuel: Pasting an anonymized log snippet: ```{
  "route":"/v1/invoke",
  "model":"rwd-opt:1.2.0-canary",
  "error":"schema_mismatch",
  "expected":"object","actual":"array",
  "sample_response":["OK"]
}```
kevin: Oof. That suggests the model variant changed output shape during generation. Could be a tokenizer/formatter diff in the new build. Does the router have an automatic fallback to permissive-route?
rita: Current routing policy sends to strict-validate variant for the canary slice. We do have a degen-route configured, but throttle and quota mapping are different — falling back would still bill as strict. Also the console alerts are surfacing as validation rejects under the strict metric which triggers accounting.
ops-sre: console-bot: Alert: validation_rejects > 3% (5m window) for route /v1/invoke in us-east-1. Notifying eng-platform.
console-bot: New dashboard tile suggestion: "Validation rejects by model_variant" — linked to traces. Would you like me to create a temporary panel? :robot_face: 
kevin: Two immediate options: 1) revert the strict-validate flag for the canary slice (fast, safe) or 2) update the router to transparently reroute failing requests to the permissive variant (requires careful quota + billing mapping). I prefer revert to stop customer impact while we debug.
samuel: Revert sounds right. Any downstream data loss or KV-cache mismatch risk if we revert mid-rollout?
rita: Reverting will move traffic back to stable variant; KV cache keys are per-model-version so no cross-risk. We'll lose the canary telemetry but that's acceptable.
kevin: I'll queue the rollback. Also: we should add a sampling hook that captures the failing responses and a small set of raw prompts so research can reproduce. Add a privacy-safe scrubber.
ops-sre: Also recommend adding a console flag to temporarily disable accounting of validation rejects during canary windows to avoid billing surprises. We can gate it with internal feature flag and a short retention.
samuel: Action items: 1) kevin -> revert strict-validate for canary (in 5m), 2) rita -> add sampling hook + scrubber, 3) kevin/ops-sre -> propose console toggle for reject-accounting. I'll own the follow-up ticket ENG-1234 and post a post-mortem if needed.
kevin: Revert started. Rolling back variant 1.2.0-canary -> 1.1.9-stable for 10% slice now. Monitoring.
rita: Added temporary sample pipeline and scrub rule. Pushed sampling config to s3://redwood-canary-samples/1749999999/
samuel: Monitoring looks good — reject rate falling back to baseline. We'll keep the canary paused until patch from model team. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
